Chapter 3: Upgrading Beliefs and Self-Image
Now that you’ve got a clear vision of where you want to go, the next step is to take a closer look at the beliefs that shape who you are—how you see yourself, and how you move through the world.
Think of your mind not as something set in stone, but more like a garden. It can be cultivated, pruned, and even replanted if you want. But here’s the thing—so many of us carry around invisible fences in that garden. Limiting beliefs about what’s possible for us. We might not even notice them, but they quietly keep us from exploring what’s beyond the familiar path.
These beliefs usually sound like internal statements: “I’m not creative,” “I’m bad with money,” or “I just don’t have what it takes to lead.” But are those really the truth? Most of the time, they’re just stories we’ve picked up—from a rough experience, a stray comment, or even what society tells us is ‘normal’. And if you hear a story enough times, you start to believe it—and live it out.
So, what can you actually do to upgrade these beliefs? Here are a few simple steps:
First, notice those patterns of negative self-talk or self-doubt that keep popping up. Pay attention to them—they’re usually trying to tell you something.
Second, try to trace those beliefs back. Where did they come from? Was it a critical teacher? Maybe a childhood setback? Or just something you absorbed from the world around you?
And then, challenge the evidence. Ask yourself: Is this belief really true? Can you find any moments—no matter how small—when the opposite was true?
Let’s say you think you’re “not a people person.” But if you look back, maybe there were times when you actually connected deeply with someone. Even if those moments were rare, they still count. Focusing on those exceptions can help you start rewriting your internal story.
Another helpful tool? Affirmations and mental rehearsal. This isn’t just repeating positive phrases in the mirror—though that can help. It’s about choosing new beliefs and practicing them until they feel real. So instead of “I’m not creative,” you might start saying, “I’m learning to express my creativity in new ways.” Pair that with small actions that reinforce this new identity, and your brain will slowly start to accept the new script.
Remember, upgrading your beliefs isn’t a one-and-done deal. Old patterns can resurface, especially when things get tough. But each time you question a limiting belief and swap it out for something more empowering, you push the boundaries of what’s possible for you. It becomes a positive cycle—new beliefs inspire new actions, which then reinforce who you’re becoming.
The real secret? Your mind is always changing. If you treat your beliefs as hypotheses—not unchangeable facts—you give yourself permission to experiment with new ways of being. That kind of flexibility is what sets extraordinary people apart. They’re willing to reinvent themselves, again and again, in the pursuit of growth and fulfillment.
So, what stories are you ready to rewrite?
